span.label: The intervention's own effect was positive but limited, and only for some students
span.note: what this limits: the size of the intervention's effect: OUR APPROACH DID HAVE A POSITIVE BUT LIMITED IMPACT ON DEVELOPING IN SOME STUDENTS A RICHER UNDERSTANDING
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The expectation held and then reversed: the motivation the design depended on appeared as predicted and did not last, which the authors report as a surprise.
span.note: what this limits: the motivational premise of this kind of intervention: the students were disturbed and motivated as assumed, but the authors report the interest was often short-lived
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The conditions the field's standard model of conceptual change rests on are reported as necessary but insufficient, with three named reasons.
span.note: what this limits: designing instruction on Posner et al.'s conditions for conceptual change: this paper quotes the position that the conditions may be necessary but are insufficient, that experiments often fail to generate the requisite data, and that cognitive limitations eclipse experimental evidence
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The evidence for the central claim is a teaching observation over five years rather than a measurement: students with undergraduate science degrees failed to generate correct predictions from a model they could otherwise manipulate, illustrated by one worked case (Archimedes' principle, floating and sinking).
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the students' own first-questionnaire answers presented back to them, confirming the degree of agreement on each answer
span.note: eliminates: the researchers' reading of a consensus that the students would not recognise - showing them their own answers is the check that the agreement is theirs
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: algorithms —distinct-from→ conceptual change
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — THE PAPER NAMES THE INFERENCE IT IS ATTACKING AND CALLS IT DECEPTIVE: 'the DECEPTIVE BELIEF that student success with algorithms and word problems leads to conceptual understanding'. The record already carries the two readings of `understanding` as senses - as the students evaluated it, and as the course required it - and this edge is the gap between them stated as a relation the paper denies.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: conceptual change —operationalised-as→ nature of science
span.note: differs in: WHICH OF THE FOUR PRECONDITIONS THE FIELD ACTUALLY ATTENDS TO: the paper notes that of Posner's four, 'the first three have been of much interest to educators'. The framework has four parts and the literature uses three · strength of the relation: 0.8
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: evidence —distinct-from→ inference
span.note: the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 1 — THE DISTINCTION IS THE PAPER'S SUBJECT AND NOTHING CARRIED IT. The record already held `algorithms -distinct-from-> conceptual change` and two readings of `understanding`, but the pair those rest on - evidence against inference - had no concept, no sense and no edge. The parenthetical IS the definition: `evidence (Nature's behavior) and inference (our models of Nature's behavior)`. Weight 1.0 because the sentence is unhedged and the goal statement at @3738 names the same distinction as objective (1) of the course.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Students answered the density/algorithm questionnaire almost perfectly, averaging 91%, and agreed strongly on the answers.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: On the conceptual floating-and-sinking questionnaire the same students averaged only 49%, close to the roughly 32% expected from random answering.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: After about six class hours of work with Archimedes' principle, nearly all students fell back on undeveloped ideas about forces and buoyancy instead of the principle when facing the finger-in-the-glass demonstration.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Of all the predictions and justifications offered in the final demonstration, exactly one invoked Archimedes' principle.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Almost all the students, despite holding undergraduate science degrees, did not understand the basic structure of science.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The motivation produced by the anomaly faded quickly, and students became frustrated at being unable to close the gap between algorithm skill and conceptual understanding fast.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Most students were glad when the floating-and-sinking unit ended, complaining that it raised more questions than answers and left some less certain of the topic than before.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
